grh_a6cf20f31366c97b47ca.title: Penny Whistle
paragraphs: This musical biography follows the frail but imaginative Robert Louis Stevenson from a childhood shaped by illness into the writer whose stories and poems reach readers around the world. His life and marriage to Fanny carry him far from Scotland, eventually to Samoa, where his health finally fails. After Stevenson's death, local islanders carry him to his mountain resting place. Fanny then reads letters from children comforted by his writing, showing that the small 'penny whistle' of his art continues to sound long after he is gone.

This [[show|the-railroad-hour|The Railroad Hour]] broadcast aired on July 6, 1953. It is listed as episode 249 in the archive. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Norman Luboff, Patricia Ianonne, Stuffy Singer, Gordon MacRae, and Lou Merrill. Other credited names include Jerome Lawrence as writer, Robert E. Lee as writer, Gordon MacRae as host, and Marvin Miller as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes. The broadcast is also associated with [[org|org.f7185f50dd01455d|Association of American Railroads]].
